_comment: Ward and notice pairs the service returns outside Karnataka, read by a person one at a time. For each body: three points inside every ward of its snapshot were put through the service's own lookup and matcher with the clock set to the day the notices were retrieved, and every pair returned was read: node infra/aws-central/tools/india-ward-runtime.mjs --pairs <STATE/city> (with --as number for a body whose index entry now says match by nothing, because this reading found its numbers wrong). Titles are the notice pack's, with a long dash written as a hyphen. tools/india-ward-runtime.mjs --write switches a snapshot on only if none of its pairs here is wrong, at most one in ten could not be told and at least ten were read.
evidence: the title itself; the zone and the name the snapshot records for a ward; every tag of every named OpenStreetMap feature inside the city's box (Geofabrik India extract, data of 6 Oct 2026); and, for the bodies listed under later_maps, a newer ward map that may not be copied, measured against and not kept

verdicts.right: the pair is the ward the work is in: the title says that ward on its own ward marker, and where the match is by number the file's numbering is shown to be the title's for that ward
verdicts.wrong: it is not, for the reason given
verdicts.cannot tell: the evidence above does not settle it

later_maps._comment: The share of a committed snapshot's area (81 points a ward) that a newer ward map gives the same ward number. Measured on 7 Oct 2026 against OpenCity files of unclear or refused licence held outside the repo; this cannot be repeated from the repo alone.
